notes: Every glb is in mm with z up, in the part's own frame; place it at `place` (three.js Euler XYZ, degrees) under its parent, the car's frame for a top-level part (D-418).
No place here is measured: every unit, the PMU, the left plate and every far end is a judgement inside its 00-CAR zone box, confirm until the dash is measured (C4, V-102, V-113).
The PMU stands for the dash node: every leg and drop meets it at the dash post (modules PMU: Dash node).
A link is a straight line from connector to connector, not the wire's run: the harness drawings (D-385) stay the wire's truth.
The boards show every part they draw, DNP ones too - the worst case the mock-ups' fit checks use.
The dash post is a cluster of receptacles beside the PMU, a row per leg (L1 at the top), 20 mm apart, each plug mated, facing the cabin - a judgement until the post is designed and measured.
The battery, disconnect, Class-T, MRBF holders and amplifier are moved to the passenger-side cargo bin (D-449); the devices builder had no node for it.

Every far end's connectors and devices stand on a shelf centred on their node, 5 mm apart (the devices 10), rows wrapping at 600 mm - a judgement, so nothing overlaps; nodes close together (the sill node and the driver kick panel) can still share space.

Each leg is a path from the dash post through judged via points inside the 00-CAR zone boxes (WAYPOINTS in export_glb.py), its radius from its conductors: 1.2 x the root of the sum of their squared diameters (TXL-class, confirm). The door drops are L4's branches through the sill node; the Audio runs (RT30-RT32) are a leg of their own from the centre stack.
The CUR's two receptacles (DP-CUR, DP-CUR-B) have no housings row yet (block 01.41): drawn from its mock-up with their plugs, no cavities.
